title: Installation Parts Kit Charge on Northgate Delivery & Installation Appointments
content:
Under Northgate Delivery & Installation, an installation appointment charges one installation parts kit for every appliance it installs, the appliances it installs being the major appliance units sold on the purchase being delivered less the major appliance units returned from it. Kits the appointment's installation parts kit entries do not yet cover are owed, and they are posted together as one installation parts kit entry dated the posting date, with the appointment's currently booked delivery date as its service date and the kits owed as its units.

The installation parts kit is the set of hoses, cords, vents or water lines the crew brings to install appliances.

## Reading the rule

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| How many kits does an installation appointment charge? | One for every appliance it installs |
| Which appliances count as installed? | The major appliance units sold on the purchase being delivered, less those returned from it |
| Which kits are owed? | Those the appointment's installation parts kit entries do not yet cover |
| How are owed kits posted? | Together, as one installation parts kit entry |
| Which dates does the entry carry? | The posting date, and the currently booked delivery date as its service date |
| What are its units? | The kits owed |

**Hypothetical appointments.** A purchase with two major appliance units sold and none returned installs two appliances. With no installation parts kit entry yet on the appointment, two kits are owed and posted together as one entry carrying 2 as its units. If an entry already covers one kit, one kit is owed.

## Posting tool: `post_installation_kit_charge_19cc3b17`

**What it does.** Member services adds one installation parts kit fee entry to a member's installation appointment for the hoses, cords, vents or water lines the crew brings to install appliances. On success the appointment's fee history shows a new installation parts kit charge for the number of kits and the amount given, posted today and tied to the appointment date given, and the amount becomes part of the delivery fees the member pays for that appointment.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool. The representative unlocks `post_installation_kit_charge_19cc3b17` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The customer reference number of the member who owns the appointment, as returned by the customer lookup and shown on the appointment | Identifier |
| `delivery_id` | The reference number of the installation appointment being charged, as returned by the delivery appointment lookup | Identifier |
| `service_date` | The appointment date the charge relates to | YYYY-MM-DD calendar date, no time or time zone; never empty |
| `kits` | The billing units of the entry: the number of installation parts kits charged | Whole positive integer |
| `amount` | The installation parts kit charge to post, in USD | 2 decimal places, always positive; stored rounded to the cent |

**Return.** On success the tool returns a description of the posted entry: `status` ("posted"), `delivery_charge_id` (the new fee entry's reference number), `delivery_id` (the appointment charged), `charge_type` (always `installation_parts_kit`), `units` (the kits charged, an integer), `amount` (the charge in USD, 2 decimal places), `event_date` (the posting date, YYYY-MM-DD) and `service_date` (the appointment date the charge relates to, YYYY-MM-DD).
